active_problem.requested_solution: SH-CS (initial requester, CL-01) asked for an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline to 1180-1260/month starting August 2026 (E-07).
Disputed bills are predominantly ACTUAL-read (1785) rather than ESTIMATED-read (1240) (E-02).
Field route completion for manual-read accounts fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target over 2026-08..09 (E-01).
Dispute response times remain within SLA, median 1.6 days vs a 3.0-day target (E-03).
No tariff rate/structure change is logged for the period (E-04).
active_problem.root_problem: Dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month to 1180-1260/month since August 2026 (E-07); disputed bills are predominantly ACTUAL-read, not estimated (1785 vs 1240, E-02), ticket response stays within SLA (E-03), and no tariff change occurred (E-04/E-06). Evidence best supports a billing import validation rule change around August 2026 causing calculation errors in issued bills regardless of read type (matching the ACTUAL-read majority and surge timing), not a response-handling, tariff, or pure estimate-substitution problem; the field route completion shortfall (E-01) is a separate smaller contributor limited to the ESTIMATED-read subset.

VOB-U-AMIACCESS.question: Is AMI register read delivery from the vendor (ORG-AMI/MDMS) degraded, contributing missing or invalid reads?

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts (9200 accounts) was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over 2026-08..09, the same window as the dispute surge, indicating a measurable shortfall in manual meter-read collection. The record shows the shortfall's existence, not its cause (staffing vs. other handoff failure).

Disputed bills break down as 1240 ESTIMATED-read and 1785 ACTUAL-read (total 3025), so the majority of disputed bills involve ACTUAL (not estimated) reads. This means estimate-substitution-based causal theories can at most explain the ESTIMATED subset (~41%), leaving the larger ACTUAL-read share unexplained by read-collection failure alone.

The CRM record shows ticket handling is currently within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs. a 3.0-day target, over 2440 tickets), indicating the surge is not a backlog/response-latency problem at present. This undercuts the premise behind CL-01's framing that an auto-answering agent addressing response speed would resolve the dispute surge; it says nothing about why bills are wrong.

The authoritative, complete billing-db tariff_change_log returns zero records, meaning no tariff rate/structure changes are logged in the system. This rules out a tariff-rule-change event as the mechanism behind any billing calculation defect, narrowing (but not eliminating) the 'billing/tariff calculation defect' theory for ACTUAL-read disputes to causes other than a logged tariff change.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a reader staffing shortage since July is causing late routes, and those late-route customers get estimated bills. This is an unverified stakeholder claim (NON_AUTHORITATIVE) offering a cause for the already-observed route completion shortfall (E-01), but it does not touch why disputed bills are predominantly ACTUAL-read (E-02).

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states there has been no tariff change this year, a stakeholder claim that agrees with the already-recorded authoritative value from E-04 (tariff_change_log has zero records). This is corroborating but non-authoritative; it adds no new mechanism and does not touch the still-unexplained ACTUAL-read dispute majority (E-02).

Monthly dispute ticket counts (610 Jun, 590 Jul, 1180 Aug, 1260 Sep) show volume roughly doubling from July to August and staying elevated in September, corroborating the magnitude/timing of the surge CL-01 describes. The record only shows aggregate ticket counts over time; it carries no information about read type, cause, or whether tickets are resolved correctly, so it does not discriminate between competing causal hypotheses.

release_summary.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS, CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and auto-fix "whatever is causing the wrong bills" after tickets roughly doubled since August (E-07). Investigation first considered field-staffing/estimation causes but E-12 showed the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills are entirely AMI-channel, not manual-read field accounts, invalidating the original problem definition (PD-1@v1). The successor problem (PD-1@v2) confirmed a different mechanism for the ESTIMATED-read subset: billing import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares raw AMI register values to m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13); v4.2 firmware meters report values in 0.1 m3 units versus legacy m3 (E-14), so BV-17 misclassifies normal consumption as high and rejects it, forcing an estimated bill that gets disputed (confirmed via E-12, E-15, E-16, E-17). This explains 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes but not the larger 1785 ACTUAL-read dispute majority. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: completed analysis deliverables within scope are released, while the BV-17 fix and the ACTUAL-read root cause are deferred as tracked, open limitations.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, SH-CS) framed the surge as a response-speed problem solvable by an auto-answering/auto-fixing AI agent, but ticket response times were within SLA (E-03), undercutting that framing (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING REJECTED).

First problem definition (PD-1@v1) attributed the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset to field-staffing/manual-read handoff failure (E-01, E-05); invalidated when E-12 showed those 1240 disputes are entirely AMI-channel (1184 rejected at import, 56 never received), not manual-read field accounts.

Confirmed mechanism (H-HIGHCONSUMP-REJECT, H-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT): rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling=none (E-13); v4.2 firmware meters report in 0.1 m3 units vs legacy m3 (E-14), causing misclassification as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, independently confirmed by four queries (E-12, E-15, E-16, E-17).
No tariff change occurred this year (E-04, corroborated by SH-BILL claim E-06/CL-03), ruling out a tariff-driven mechanism.

Release scope (SD-2) covered analyzing the billing import-rule log (DA-RULES), AMI read events (DA-MDMS), and dispute tickets by read type (DA-TICKET); these were completed (W-AMI-READS, W-DISPUTE-IMPORTSTATUS-V42 both DONE).
No automated bill writes occurred (gated by K-BILLWRITE, requiring SH-BILL authorization) and no field dispatch route change occurred (gated by K-DISPATCH, requiring SH-FIELD runtime confirmation).
Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds; DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs).
limitations_explained: The larger ACTUAL-read dispute majority (1785 of 3025 disputed bills, E-02) is not explained by the confirmed BV-17/unit-scaling mechanism; its cause remains unknown and is tracked as the open, CRITICAL unknown U-ACTUALCAUSE / VOB-U-ACTUALCAUSE, explicitly excluded from this release's scope.

The actual fix for BV-17 (applying firmware-aware unit scaling via billing-config change control, SR-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING) was judged not feasible within contest time; the defect in BV-17 itself remains uncorrected.

Already-issued incorrect bills tied to the 1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION accounts have not been corrected; manual re-billing (SR-MANUAL-REBILL-AFFECTED) was judged infeasible in available time and would still require manual Billing Operations review/authorization under K-BILLWRITE.

A proposed metric improvement (SR-DISAGGREGATE-METRIC) was not pursued as a release item; even if done, it would only improve measurement validity and would not itself reduce disputes or correct any bill.

The field route completion shortfall's cause (staffing shortage vs. another handoff failure, unknown U-FIELDCAUSE) remains open and unresolved, though it is no longer believed to contribute to the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset.

output.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS, CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and auto-fix "whatever is causing the wrong bills" after tickets roughly doubled since August (E-07). Investigation first considered field-staffing/estimation causes but E-12 showed the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills are entirely AMI-channel, not manual-read field accounts, invalidating the original problem definition (PD-1@v1). The successor problem (PD-1@v2) confirmed a different mechanism for the ESTIMATED-read subset: billing import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares raw AMI register values to m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13); v4.2 firmware meters report values in 0.1 m3 units versus legacy m3 (E-14), so BV-17 misclassifies normal consumption as high and rejects it, forcing an estimated bill that gets disputed (confirmed via E-12, E-15, E-16, E-17). This explains 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes but not the larger 1785 ACTUAL-read dispute majority. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: completed analysis deliverables within scope are released, while the BV-17 fix and the ACTUAL-read root cause are deferred as tracked, open limitations.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, SH-CS) framed the surge as a response-speed problem solvable by an auto-answering/auto-fixing AI agent, but ticket response times were within SLA (E-03), undercutting that framing (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING REJECTED).

First problem definition (PD-1@v1) attributed the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset to field-staffing/manual-read handoff failure (E-01, E-05); invalidated when E-12 showed those 1240 disputes are entirely AMI-channel (1184 rejected at import, 56 never received), not manual-read field accounts.

Confirmed mechanism (H-HIGHCONSUMP-REJECT, H-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT): rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling=none (E-13); v4.2 firmware meters report in 0.1 m3 units vs legacy m3 (E-14), causing misclassification as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, independently confirmed by four queries (E-12, E-15, E-16, E-17).
No tariff change occurred this year (E-04, corroborated by SH-BILL claim E-06/CL-03), ruling out a tariff-driven mechanism.

Release scope (SD-2) covered analyzing the billing import-rule log (DA-RULES), AMI read events (DA-MDMS), and dispute tickets by read type (DA-TICKET); these were completed (W-AMI-READS, W-DISPUTE-IMPORTSTATUS-V42 both DONE).
No automated bill writes occurred (gated by K-BILLWRITE, requiring SH-BILL authorization) and no field dispatch route change occurred (gated by K-DISPATCH, requiring SH-FIELD runtime confirmation).
Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds; DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs).
limitations_explained: The larger ACTUAL-read dispute majority (1785 of 3025 disputed bills, E-02) is not explained by the confirmed BV-17/unit-scaling mechanism; its cause remains unknown and is tracked as the open, CRITICAL unknown U-ACTUALCAUSE / VOB-U-ACTUALCAUSE, explicitly excluded from this release's scope.

The actual fix for BV-17 (applying firmware-aware unit scaling via billing-config change control, SR-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING) was judged not feasible within contest time; the defect in BV-17 itself remains uncorrected.

Already-issued incorrect bills tied to the 1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION accounts have not been corrected; manual re-billing (SR-MANUAL-REBILL-AFFECTED) was judged infeasible in available time and would still require manual Billing Operations review/authorization under K-BILLWRITE.

A proposed metric improvement (SR-DISAGGREGATE-METRIC) was not pursued as a release item; even if done, it would only improve measurement validity and would not itself reduce disputes or correct any bill.

The field route completion shortfall's cause (staffing shortage vs. another handoff failure, unknown U-FIELDCAUSE) remains open and unresolved, though it is no longer believed to contribute to the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset.
